_doc: Crew profiles: which model and effort does each kind of work. Pick one with "profile" in .crew\config.json (or CREW_PROFILE, or route.ps1 -Set). Override single entries with "routing": { "<kind>": { "who": "sonnet", "effort": "high" } }. who = worker (the cheap API model) | haiku | sonnet | opus. Security and tier 3 work are never routed below opus.

models.worker: Fast and cheap (DeepSeek V4.x by default). Strong at clear-spec code, tests, mechanical fixes and reading diffs. Weak at open design decisions and visual taste: every vague word in a brief becomes a guess.
models.haiku: Fast, cheapest Claude. Good for small, clear reviews, scouting and summaries. Not for design or security judgement.
models.sonnet: The workhorse. Strong implementation, UI and visual polish, debugging and thorough code review at a fraction of opus cost.
models.opus: The deepest reasoning. Architecture and planning, security, money and auth code, hard bugs, final review of critical or key work.

kinds.orchestrator: the main session: briefs, dispatch, merges (a recommendation; set it in the host)
kinds.plan: decompose a feature into units (Full mode)
kinds.brief_check: goldfish review of each brief before dispatch (brief-check.ps1)
kinds.scout: map files and call sites before planning
kinds.build_t2: complex: algorithms, concurrency, performance paths, heavy logic
kinds.build_t3: critical: auth, crypto, money, FFI, security boundaries (tests first by the worker)
kinds.build_ui: a new or redesigned screen whose look matters (tests first by the worker)
kinds.review_ui: Gate 3 for a UI unit, with the screenshot
kinds.security: nexus-sentinel on anything touching auth, secrets, input handling, payments
kinds.debug: a failure whose cause is unknown, or a unit that escalated twice

premium.summary: Best result first. Claude builds the hard and visible parts, every unit gets a deep review, workers get more room to think. Highest cost, fewest regressions.

balanced.summary: The default. Workers build everything with a clear spec, Claude builds screens people look at and critical code, and reviews scale with the tier.

economy.summary: Lowest cost. Workers build all non-critical work including UI (with a visual check), Claude reviews low tiers in one batched pass, and Opus is kept for critical and security work only.
economy.review_style: one batched review for tier 0-1 units, per-unit from tier 2
economy.visual_check: UI units, before Gate 3; a rejected screen moves up to sonnet/medium
